messages:
maya: Quick q — can we define routing that prefers v2 but falls back to v1 per-customer without breaking quota/accounting? thinking about gradual rollouts + tenant exemptions

alex: yes, we can. two parts: 1) routing decision (prefer v2) 2) quota attribution (must tag requests with effective-version)

sam: agree. we should avoid changing token billing semantics. suggestion: inject `x-effective-api-version: v1|v2` at ingress and use that for quota/metrics. keep `x-client-api-version` untouched for client visibility

liz: console UX question — if we auto-fallback, how do we surface it? customers will want to know when they hit v1 so they can fix clients. propose a per-route toggle in Console: "show fallbacks" with sample traces + last-fallback timestamp

maya: +1. also need a lightweight probe to sample who actually falls back. maybe 1% of requests per customer flagged for full trace

alex: implementation sketch — router evaluates order: pinned-version > client-header > policy-grid > default. if chosen version not available, fallback to compatible variant and add header `x-fallback-reason: capacity|incompat|error`

sam: small code snippet for header negotiation we used in proxy:
```
# pseudo-proxy rule
if client.headers['x-client-api-version'] == 'v2':
  route = try_route('v2')
  if !route:
    route = route('v1')
    set_header('x-fallback-reason','unavailable')
    set_header('x-effective-api-version','v1')
else:
  route = default_route()
```

liz: important: quota must be charged against the effective model served, not the client header. otherwise usage graphs lie and customers get billed unexpectedly

maya: operational question — do we count a fallback as an error for SLOs? i lean toward counting only when result incompatible (e.g., schema mismatch). capacity fallbacks should be visible but not a hard error

ops-bot: [telemetry] New metric proposal: `api.version.fallback.count` with tags: tenant_id, from_version, to_version, reason. TTL retention 90d. alert if 5xx-fallback-rate > 0.5% over 15m

deploy-bot: rolling deploy queued for `v2-router` -> canary 5% -> 2026-03-20T22:10Z. will emit `router.canary.started` events

alex: rollout plan idea: enable auto-fallback by default in platform but opt-out per-tenant via Console flag. during canary: enable fallback sampling + telemetry export to `incidents` stream

sam: edge case: what about function/tool-calling model outputs where v2 has structured responses and v1 doesn't? fallback could silently break integrations. we need an explicit inference-level compatibility matrix per model pair

liz: yep — add a warning banner in Console for tenant if any `fallback` happened and the to_version < expected_structured_support

maya: decision-ish: implement headers (`x-effective-api-version`, `x-fallback-reason`), count quota against effective-version, add `api.version.fallback.count` metric, expose per-tenant fallback toggle + sample traces in Console. we'll still require a model-pair compatibility matrix before broad auto-fallback enablement

alex: can someone file infra ticket to add header propagation at edge + a migration job to backfill metrics? (sam?)

sam: filing now — INC-2026-237: add `x-effective-api-version` propagation, fallback metric, and sampling traces. I'll include the compatibility matrix schema proposal

maya: thanks. small follow-up: update docs/FAQ and quickstart so customers know what to expect if their client pins v1 but platform prefers v2 (and vice versa). also add console explainer for "Why did I see v1 responses?"

liz: i'll take the Console copy + banner mocks. dropping a sketch in #design later today :pencil2: 

ops-bot: [note] alerting rule queued: high fallback-rate -> page on-call SRE if >1% for 10m and trending up

deploy-bot: canary started (5%). router.canary.id=rc-2026-78

maya: perfect. let's sync tomorrow in standup to confirm tickets and ownership. thanks all :thumbsup:
